key_insight: Learning latent world models at multiple temporal scales enables hierarchical planning that reduces prediction error accumulation and search complexity, allowing effective long-horizon control with learned models.
problem_solved: Mitigates long-horizon failures of learned world models caused by compounding prediction errors and exponentially growing planning search spaces, improving zero-shot generalization to new environments.
method: Learn latent dynamics models at multiple temporal resolutions (short-horizon fine model + longer-horizon coarse models) to compress predictions and reduce error propagation.
Perform hierarchical planning: a high-level planner searches in coarse latent space for long-range subgoals, while a low-level MPC/controller executes and refines actions in fine latent dynamics.
Use latent rollouts and goal-conditioned control to connect levels, enabling efficient coarse-to-fine search and robust execution despite model imperfections.
impact: Provides a practical approach for scaling model-based control to long-horizon tasks, improving sample efficiency and generalization for robotics and embodied AI. Practitioners can integrate temporal abstraction into learned models to make planning tractable and robust.
visual_elements: Schematic of hierarchical architecture: stacked latent models (coarse → fine) with arrows showing high-level planner producing subgoals and low-level MPC executing actions.
Timeline/temporal abstraction diagram showing different prediction horizons for each latent model and how errors accumulate less at coarse scales.
Performance chart comparing success rate or planning cost vs horizon for single-scale world model vs hierarchical latent models.
Flowchart of planning loop: observe → encode to latents → high-level plan → low-level MPC → execute → replan.
paper_title: Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models
paper_authors: Wancong Zhang, Basile Terver, Artem Zholus, Soham Chitnis, Harsh Sutaria
